title: Sector 5 is THE SIDE WALL: a breach comes up beside the gate inside the front sentries' reach, cuts a lane through the rim and breaks the wall there, and Isao prints the wall shut once the lane is quiet, on a grown base or a static one
context: Owner, 2026-10-01: "after 4 waves there's a « side breach ». Problem, but still within range of some of the existing towers so easier to manage. This is a chekov's gun of sorts, it reveals that the walls can be breached." The second step after 2026-10-01-the-ramp-before-the-back-door, which left sector 5 a plain gate-side sector. In the owner's words WALL is the printed kit segments flanking the gate (ROCK is the lattice). A breach's own blast clears every rock cell within six cells, which beside the base would open the whole rim (the reason sector placement keeps breaches ten cells off it). On the real planet the six wall cells sit just inside the clearing with rim rock behind them; the Rotor's and the Quiver's sockets are beside the lane, 2.7 to 4 cells from the gate.
outcome: src/domain/side-breach.js (new) lists where it can come up: open ground outside the clearing 2.5 to 5 cells from the nearest wall cell, within 3.5 cells of a sentry socket, at least 3.5 from the gate; each with the lane it cuts (walked through the rock to the wall, one cell wide) and two wall cells; a lane through the gate's mouth or a socket is no candidate (on the story planet four remain, all by the wall three cells from the gate, 1.3 to 3 cells from a socket). SECTORS[4] is THE SIDE WALL, { side: 1, gate: 1 }, side first. src/fx/sector-run.js places it from storyApi.sideBreachCandidates (src/fx/programme-host.js), falls back to the gate side without one, opens it with its own blast radius (0.6 cells: td-tab's breach takes obj.userData.clear) and breakSide breaks the lane's rock and the wall cells (breachWallCell) and drops every kit segment on them (src/fx/story-base.js dropWallsAt); THE WALL IS BREACHED and Isao's side_breach line. story.wallCells is now every wall cell (it held only pending ones, empty on a static base), restoreWall raises every segment on a cell, and a static base's programme host runs its repairs before refusing new steps, so Isao mends a broken wall or a chewed gate on the SKIP ALL base too. tankSight's visible-band test reuses viewEdge to pay for the controller's share.
alternatives: The breach's own six-cell blast beside the wall: takes the rim, the walls and any unmounted socket with it; not 'easier to manage'.
Breaking bowl rock instead of the wall: Isao mends walls, not rock, so the hole would stay for every later sector and bypass the gate.
evidence: test/side-breach.mjs (new): candidates in reach, the lane and the gap, never through the gate or a socket. test/sector-run.mjs: sector 5 places the side breach first, its small blast, the wall broken, Isao's line; no candidate falls back to two gate breaches. test/programme-host.mjs: a static base sends Isao to mend a broken wall. test/sectors.mjs: the table.
